Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "Our family photo catalogue is a shared spreadsheet that my sister Lena and I update together. We started it after finding several boxes of prints in our grandmother’s hall cupboard. The first entries cover the years from 1968 to 1982, and we have added newer pictures whenever someone can identify the people and place.

Each row records the date, location, names, and the box or album where the original can be found. If we are unsure about a detail, we mark it as uncertain rather than guessing. Last Sunday, Lena brought over a small envelope of photographs from a seaside holiday in 1976. Our uncle Martin recognized the hotel sign in the background, so we added the town name and noted that he had identified it. One picture shows three children beside a striped deck chair, but nobody yet knows which child is our mother. We left that name field blank and attached a note asking the family to check with her.

The catalogue is useful because it keeps the information with the images without pretending that every memory is certain. We also keep the original prints in numbered sleeves, so a family member can find one without handling the whole box.", "output": "Our family photo catalogue is a shared spreadsheet that my sister Lena and I update together. Each row records the date, location, names, and the box or album where the original can be found. If we are unsure about a detail, we mark it as uncertain rather than guessing. Last Sunday, Lena brought over a small envelope of photographs from a seaside holiday in 1976. Our uncle Martin recognized the hotel sign in the background, so we added the town name and noted that he had identified it. One picture shows three children beside a striped deck chair, but nobody yet knows which child is our mother. We left that name field blank and attached a note asking the family to check with her.

The catalogue is useful because it keeps the information with the images without pretending that every memory is certain. We also keep the original prints in numbered sleeves, so a family member can find one without handling the whole box."}]
